business_problem: In 2019 and 2022, Foursquare completed a two-stage cloud migration, transferring its open-source data pipelines to Amazon EMR , a cloud big data solution for petabyte-scale data processing, interactive analytics, and machine learning using open-source frameworks.
solution_summary: Processing large quantities of data can take considerable time and resources. Foursquare , a geospatial technology company responsible for processing billions of location data points daily, sought a way to streamline productivity by simplifying its cluster management. Overall, Foursquare’s use of Amazon EMR Serverless reduced costs by 45 percent. Learn how Foursquare, a geospatial technology company, modernized their data analytics applications and reduced costs and operational overhead using Amazon EMR Serverless. By deploying Amazon EMR Serverless —a service that makes it simple for data analysts and engineers to run open-source big data analytics frameworks without configuring, managing, and scaling clusters or servers—Foursquare reduced operational overhead and increased developer productivity. architecture_clues: The primary driver behind Foursquare’s modernization with Amazon EMR Serverless was productivity optimizations, but the company also achieved significant cost savings. “Amazon EMR Serverless allocates just enough RAM CPU and can spin up or down faster than instances, so you get more efficient usage, which saves money,” says Joseph.
Overall, Foursquare’s use of Amazon EMR Serverless reduced costs by 45 percent.
The modernization to a serverless AWS solution also increased staff productivity.

Using Amazon EMR Serverless removes the need to define instance types, so Foursquare’s developers can spend more time scrubbing user data as it’s collected and less time dealing with cluster settings and other granular optimizations. “There is a lot of efficiency to be gained by the rapid scaling and the rightsizing of clusters that happens automatically with Amazon EMR Serverless,” says Joseph.
